newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down, contango widens.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down, contango widens.

text.p: The Singapore gas oil swaps edged down late afternoon on Thursday on concerns of a prompt physical overhang as the inter-front months contango deepened, traders said.
"Gas oil came off slightly this afternoon because of the concerns of surplus physical cargoes but there has not been much trading," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $24.50/$24.60 per barrel while July was at $24.60/$24.70, down five and 15 cents from Wednesday's quotes, respectively, brokers said.
The June/July spread traded earlier in the day minus 3 cents, they said.
Traders said soft June swaps was due to market concerns over the surplus prompt cargoes in Singapore and lack of Chinese purchases amid reports of several distressed cargoes in North Asia.

In the Singapore physical market, sellers emerged late Wednesday to offer their barrels aggressively and 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $24.50 per barrel for June 19-23 lifting, down 40 cents from Tuesday's offered level for a cargo loading at similar dates.
Offers for end June/early July barrels were also lower at $24.80 per barrel from Tuesday's traded level of $25.30 per barrel.
Traders said sellers lowered their offers sharply due to both weaker crude and the absence of regional enduser demand.
In China there are up to four prompt cargoes of around 30,000 tonnes each still unsold.
The market is also concerned over the shipment of up to four 60,000 to 80,0000 tonne tankers from the Mediterranean and Black Sea headed to this region for arrival in early July.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted almost unchanged from Wednesday at $100.50/$101.25.
